title: Simple Attribute
description: Treat a property as one domain value for the application’s purposes, distinguish simplicity from multiplicity and derivation, and query complete values without invented decomposition rules.
notes:
## Simple means one modeled value

A simple attribute is treated as one value without separately modeled subcomponents for the application's relevant operations. A student's registration code can be a simple attribute when the system stores and compares it as an opaque identifier. The code may contain letters and digits, but individual characters do not automatically become separate properties in the entity model.

The choice follows required meaning and operations. A catalogue application may display an entire contact label without querying its parts. Another application may need a structured address with separately maintained city and postal code. Neither choice is determined solely by the number of characters. State what the system needs to recognize, validate, compare, or update before deciding that a property is simple or composite.

## Atomic does not mean physically indivisible

A date has calendar components, a string has characters, and a decimal number has a representation. These facts do not automatically make every attribute composite. The modeled domain can still treat a date or identifier as one value. Atomicity is not a claim that no program could ever inspect the value's representation or apply a supported function to it.

An SQL date function can extract a year from a stored date without requiring the conceptual model to describe separate birth-year, birth-month, and birth-day attributes. Likewise, a string comparison can operate on an identifier without treating its prefix as an independent business field. Keep the chosen domain value separate from every possible operation an implementation can perform on its representation.

## Requirements can justify decomposition

Suppose an address must support city-specific delivery reports and independent postal-code validation. A composite Address with meaningful components can express those needs clearly. If the system only displays a supplied mailing label and must preserve its formatting, decomposing that label by guessed spaces or commas can lose information. The representation should preserve the actual contract rather than enforce an arbitrary parsing assumption.

Names require similar care. Not every person's name follows a universal first-name and last-name pattern. Treating a display name as one property can be appropriate when separate components are unnecessary. If independent name fields are required, their semantics and accepted cultural variations need a deliberate policy. Simplicity is a modeling choice that should respect the facts and users being represented.

## Simple does not imply numeric

Registration codes, status labels, and supported dates can be simple attributes under their documented domains. A numeric type is neither required nor sufficient. A long identifier with leading zeros may need a string representation because it is not a quantity. Converting it to an integer can discard distinctions the issuing policy considers meaningful.

Choose the domain and SQL type from the role. A postal code used as an opaque identifier does not become an amount merely because its current values contain digits. Arithmetic on it may be meaningless. A simple numeric score, by contrast, can support valid arithmetic under the specified scale. Shared representation does not imply shared semantics or interchangeable values.

## Multiplicity answers a different question

A simple phone value can occur several times for one student if the model permits multiple phone numbers. Each phone is treated as one value, while the property as a whole is multivalued. Simplicity describes internal modeled structure; single-valued or multivalued describes how many simultaneous values can belong to an occurrence. The two dimensions should not be collapsed into one classification.

A single structured address can be composite yet single-valued. Several structured addresses can be composite and multivalued. A simple registration identifier can be single-valued and required. These combinations illustrate why a diagram or exercise needs the relevant assumptions stated explicitly. One classification label does not automatically settle all the other properties of an attribute.

## Derivation is independent too

A calculated total can be represented as one simple result value even when it is derived from several source facts. A stored registration code can also be simple. Derived versus stored concerns where the property comes from, not whether it has separately modeled components. Avoid a multiple-choice explanation implying that age cannot be simple merely because it is calculated.

A derived value still needs a correct rule, units, population, and reference point. Age at a stated date differs from a timeless stored integer. A credit total over completed registrations differs from a count of all proposed registrations. Calling the output simple does not validate its calculation; that remains a separate part of the property contract.

## A scalar mapping can use one column

A straightforward mapping can store a simple single-valued property in one column alongside the entity identifier. An explicit projection can return the complete value rather than decomposing it into arbitrary character positions. This keeps the result aligned with the domain's opaque-identifier policy and avoids accidentally treating a prefix as an independently meaningful entity property.

```sql
SELECT student_id, registration_code
FROM students
WHERE registration_code = 'CS-007'
ORDER BY student_id;
```

The query compares the complete supplied code under the applicable column comparison rules. It does not infer campus, programme, or admission year from pieces of the string. If a real issuing specification assigns such components and the application needs them, that is a different documented model. A similar-looking sample pattern alone is insufficient evidence to invent those semantics.

## Domain constraints still apply

Simple attributes are not exempt from required-value, range, format, or reference policies. An opaque code can be required and unique under a particular scope. A status can be limited to a maintained set. A simple date can need an appropriate validity range. The classification explains one aspect of representation rather than proving that every possible input is legal.

Missing information also needs definition. An optional contact token can be NULL under an SQL mapping, while an empty string is a distinct recorded value. COALESCE can supply a result-only fallback for absence without changing the source. Do not store the same ordinary placeholder into a required unique identifier field merely to make missing values look complete; that changes both semantics and possible uniqueness behaviour.

## Components can be nested before reaching simple leaves

A composite property can contain another composite component. Address might contain a structured location, which in turn contains city and region. The ultimate leaves can be simple attributes even when every immediate component at the top level is not simple. It is therefore inaccurate to state that composite attributes can only have simple immediate children.

This matters when mapping a nested conceptual structure into relational columns. Identify the leaf roles needed for the implementation and preserve their meanings. A large nested JSON object or an arbitrary split string is not automatically the same as a well-defined ER decomposition. The conceptual model and chosen SQL representation should be explained separately and kept consistent.

A complete-value query can also preserve two different entities sharing the same optional contact token when the model permits sharing. Do not add DISTINCT merely to make the display shorter if the requested grain is one student. Simplicity says how the token is modeled; it does not supply uniqueness or decide whether shared contact values are legitimate.

## Query and validate complete values deliberately

Fixtures can include two codes sharing a prefix, an identifier with leading zeros, a missing optional token, and repeated descriptive names. Check that equality matches the intended complete value and that unrelated similar-looking values remain distinct under the documented comparison policy. Keep entity identifiers in result rows so descriptive repetition does not collapse different occurrences.

The exercises use canonical code spellings and ordinary lowercase contact tokens to avoid unstated collation edge cases. They demonstrate complete-value selection and result-only absence handling on isolated SQL data. They do not establish a universal identifier parser, external issuance truth, or production access rights. A useful simple-attribute explanation preserves the chosen domain value while making clear which structure, multiplicity, and derivation decisions remain independent.

questions.question_text: What is a simple (atomic) attribute?
options: An attribute that can take multiple values for one entity
A property treated as one domain value without separately modeled components for the application’s purposes
An attribute derived from other attributes
An attribute that is always numeric
questions.explanation: Simple does not mean that a representation has no characters, date components or conceivable internal operations.

questions.question_text: Which is a simple attribute under a model that treats Roll_No as an opaque code and models Address components separately?
options: Address (Street, City, State, Pincode)
Roll_No
Phone_Numbers (a list of numbers)
Address with separately modeled city and postal code
questions.explanation: The question states the modeled component policy; derivation and simplicity are separate dimensions.

questions.question_text: Why can Address be modeled as composite when city and postal code need independent management?
options: Because it is always stored as a single VARCHAR column
Because it naturally decomposes into meaningful independent sub-parts like Street, City, State, and Pincode
Because it is a multi-valued attribute
Because it is a derived attribute
questions.explanation: Address breaks into City/State/etc., which are individually useful — the defining trait of a composite attribute, unlike a simple attribute.

questions.question_text: Is whether an attribute is simple or composite an absolute, fixed property of real-world data?
options: Yes, it never depends on application requirements
No — it is a design decision based on whether sub-parts need to be queried or referenced independently
Yes, but only for weak entities
No, all attributes are composite by default
questions.explanation: The same real-world value (e.g., Name) can be modeled as simple or composite depending on application needs.

questions.question_text: Can a simple attribute also be multi-valued?
options: No, simple and multi-valued are mutually exclusive by definition
Yes — e.g., Phone_Number can be indivisible as a unit (simple) while a student can still have several of them (multi-valued)
Only composite attributes can be multi-valued
Only derived attributes can be multi-valued
questions.explanation: Simplicity (structural indivisibility) and single/multi-valued (occurrence count) are independent classification axes.

questions.question_text: When a composite property is recursively decomposed into leaf roles, what can those leaves be?
options: Other composite attributes only
Relationships
Simple attributes, even though intermediate components may themselves be composite
Derived attributes only
questions.explanation: Nested composition is possible; not every immediate component must already be a simple leaf.

questions.question_text: A database that never needs to query the local-part or domain of an email separately would model `Email` as:
options: Composite
Multi-valued
Simple
Derived
questions.explanation: Without a need to reference sub-parts, Email is treated as a single indivisible (simple) attribute.

questions.question_text: Which statement about simple attributes is FALSE?
options: They have no meaningful sub-parts for the application's purposes
They can never appear as part of a composite attribute
Their classification as 'simple' depends on the application's querying needs
CGPA and Gender are typical examples
questions.explanation: Simple attributes are exactly what composite attributes are composed of, so this statement is false.

questions.question_text: Does a date having calendar components automatically forbid treating it as one simple domain value?
options: Yes; every date must become three entity attributes
No; the modeled role can still be one date
Only if the date is missing
Only if stored as text
questions.explanation: Representation structure and conceptual decomposition differ.

questions.question_text: Can a simple attribute also be derived?
options: No; calculated values are never attributes
Only if no source data exists
Yes; derivation and structural decomposition are separate dimensions
Only if it is multivalued
questions.explanation: A computed total can still be one simple output value.

questions.question_text: Why preserve CS-007 as a code rather than blindly converting it to a number?
options: All codes support meaningful addition
Leading zeros always mean NULL
Its documented identifier representation can matter
Only integers can be keys
questions.explanation: An identifier need not be a quantity.

questions.question_text: What evidence justifies inferring programme from a registration-code prefix?
options: A similar-looking sample alone
The first character on screen
A short alias
A documented issuing and modeling contract requiring that component
questions.explanation: Do not invent semantics from a visual pattern.

questions.question_text: Can several simple phone values belong to one student?
options: Yes, under a multivalued-phone policy
No; simple implies one occurrence
Only if phone values are numbers
Only if the student has no identity
questions.explanation: Multiplicity and structural simplicity differ.

questions.question_text: Why might a display name remain one simple attribute?
options: Every name must contain exactly two words
Separate components may be unnecessary or inconsistent with the accepted naming policy
Simple names must be unique
A string can never be queried
questions.explanation: The representation follows actual application needs.

questions.question_text: Does a simple attribute need no validation?
options: Yes; atomic values are automatically true
Only if it contains digits
No; its domain and absence policies still apply
Only if it is derived
questions.explanation: Classification does not establish value validity.

questions.question_text: What does a COALESCE fallback in SELECT do?
options: It splits the token into components
It always replaces empty strings too
It changes every key
It supplies an output value for NULL without updating the source
questions.explanation: Presentation expressions are distinct from writes and decomposition.

questions.question_text: Can a composite attribute contain another composite component?
options: Yes; decomposition can be nested
No; immediate children must always be simple
Only if keys are absent
Only if stored as one integer
questions.explanation: Simple attributes can be the ultimate leaves.

questions.question_text: Which fixture challenges an accidental prefix-only code lookup?
options: Only one code
Two different complete codes sharing the same prefix
No source table
A colour label
questions.explanation: The query must follow complete-value semantics.

questions.question_text: What must a derived simple value still specify?
options: Only its displayed colour
Only the source filename
Its calculation rule, units and reference population or point
Only the code prefix
questions.explanation: Simplicity does not prove the arithmetic is meaningful.

questions.question_text: What distinguishes simple from composite in this context?
options: How many characters the value has
Whether it is numeric
Whether every student has one
Whether useful subcomponents are modeled separately
questions.explanation: Application meaning and operations drive the distinction.

coding_problems.title: Match one complete opaque registration code
coding_problems.task: Return student_id and registration_code where the complete code equals CS-007. Do not match CS-070 or CS-007-X.
coding_problems.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, registration_code VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, contact_token VARCHAR(50) NULL);
constraints: Registration codes are opaque complete identifiers in this exercise.
Fixture spellings avoid collation-sensitive distinctions; contact absence is NULL, not an empty string.
edge_cases: Similar code prefixes do not imply equality.
An empty contact string remains an ordinary stored value.
hints: Compare the complete code when the contract asks for it.
Use absence predicates and result expressions deliberately.
coding_problems.solution_sql: SELECT student_id, registration_code FROM students WHERE registration_code = 'CS-007' ORDER BY student_id;
coding_problems.explanation: The query respects complete domain values and the stated absence contract without inventing internal code components.

coding_problems.title: Describe whether each simple contact value was supplied
coding_problems.task: Return student_id and contact_state: missing if contact_token is NULL, empty if it is the empty string, otherwise supplied. These labels describe presence only and do not validate token ownership.
coding_problems.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, registration_code VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, contact_token VARCHAR(50) NULL);
constraints: Registration codes are opaque complete identifiers in this exercise.
Fixture spellings avoid collation-sensitive distinctions; contact absence is NULL, not an empty string.
edge_cases: Similar code prefixes do not imply equality.
An empty contact string remains an ordinary stored value.
hints: Compare the complete code when the contract asks for it.
Use absence predicates and result expressions deliberately.
coding_problems.solution_sql: SELECT student_id, CASE WHEN contact_token IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN contact_token = '' THEN 'empty' ELSE 'supplied' END AS contact_state FROM students ORDER BY student_id;
coding_problems.explanation: The query respects complete domain values and the stated absence contract without inventing internal code components.
